body:
Single release candidate for the private family beta. **Not ready to merge: NO-GO.** Draft, because the two things outstanding are ones code cannot close — human content approval, and the DEV credentials for the hosted rollout.

Authoritative checklist: `docs/runbooks/family-beta-rollout-checklist.md`. Per-item content worksheet: `docs/content-status/family-beta-approval-manifest.md`.

## What this reconciles

- PRs **#91** (`ed52ef99`), **#93** (`75549435`), **#94** (`46592735`) — each re-fetched and confirmed an ancestor, so none moved since it was merged. `origin/dev` (`17d8be2f`) contained.
- `feat/family-beta-fixed-papers` (`5cfa3555`), which had diverged: the pinned-paper loader, the pinned data, the Year 5 Q24 payment-wording correction (diff byte-identical to `23a7586b`), and the fixed-paper/interactive-renderer tests.
- The brief named `759fadbe`; the branch was already at `d5bd9a25`, with `759fadbe` an ancestor. Nothing lost.

## Defects found and fixed

- **RLS (the one CI failure on the first pushed SHA).** `tests/rls/target-http-lifecycle.test.ts` scoped `EXAM_WRITE_DB_URL` to the loopback writer but not `EXAM_WRITE_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`, so `validatedTarget()` refused with `loopback_not_enabled` before connecting and three legacy-model expectations saw 503 instead of 200. **No control weakened** — `exam-write-target.test.ts` still proves a loopback target is refused without the flag, and a hosted one on a ref mismatch. Green on Linux.
- **Accessibility, found and fixed app-wide.** `BarChartRenderer` was the only chart renderer with no accessible data equivalent — every mark `aria-hidden`, only `altText` — so any bar-chart item whose alt text doesn't recite its values was unanswerable without sight. It now carries the same `sr-only` data list `LineGraphRenderer` already had, with two tests.
- **Gate hardening.** `isFamilyBetaFixedPapersEnabled()` checked only `VERCEL_TARGET_ENV`; `VERCEL_ENV` is the only production signal on older Vercel builds, so a production deployment with the flag set could have served unapproved content. Both refused now.
- **Navigation.** CI's `navigation-graph` test caught that the new reviewer index had no way out (all links were template literals). Fixed; route now listed on `/dev/routes`.
- **Fixture isolation.** `stripe-webhook-route.test.ts` threw `ENOENT` on a gitignored `.env.local`, so the suite failed to collect in any worktree (0 of 8 tests ran). CI was never affected. Synthetic fallback after the existing lookups; no assertion changed.

## CI gaps that made a green run prove less than it looked

- **20 of 90 authenticated tests were skipping — the entire email-confirmation and password-recovery path** (`E2E_MAILPIT_URL` unset, though `supabase start` runs the catcher on 56324). Now set: **skipped went 20 → 0** and those tests pass.
- **The ×5 keyboard repeat watched the wrong spec.** The real flake was the public sign-in walkthrough; the repeat covered the parent dashboard, which never flaked. A public repeat was added — **10/10 with `--retries=0`**, so that flake is not a reproducible defect.
- **The core student journey was flaky once** (`student-exam-session.spec.ts`: code+PIN sign-in, timed exam, autosave, resume). A retry-pass is not adequate evidence for the journey both children take, so a `student exam journey ×5, retries 0` step now runs it, gated by `--require-spec`, in the final gate.

## Evidence

`family-beta-verify` passed on Linux three times. Run of record `99127c60` was **completely clean**:

| | Authenticated | Public | Repeats, retries off |
|---|---|---|---|
| `50916415` | 69 passed, 0 failed, 1 flaky, **20 skipped** | 385 passed, 0 failed, 1 flaky | kbd 5/5 |
| `a34fd6f8` | 89 passed, 0 failed, 1 flaky, 0 skipped | 385 passed, 0 failed, 1 flaky | kbd 5/5, public kbd 10/10 |
| `99127c60` | **90/90, 0 flaky, 0 skipped** | **386/386, 0 flaky, 0 skipped** | kbd 5/5, public kbd 10/10 |

CI on `99127c60`: `rls`, `e2e`, `e2e-auth`, `scholarship-drafts` passed; `core` failed on the navigation-graph omission above, since fixed. Locally on the final SHA: typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, build clean, **406/406 suites and 7142/7142 tests pass**, all content/ledger/answer checks pass.

No failure was hidden by a retry, a skipped assertion or a raised timeout; both flakes were named, and each was either disproved by repetition or put under it. Windows E2E remains invalid and no Windows count is quoted.

## Content

- **78/78 pins verified**: every `canonicalSha256` recomputed with the repo's `hashJson` and matched; types, slot sequence, id uniqueness agree. Y3 36 items/36 marks, Y5 42 items/49 marks.
- **All 78 answer keys independently solved by hand: 78/78 correct**, including the corrected Y5 Q24.
- No answer leakage in candidate delivery; scoring server-side.
- **Partial and unanswered scoring now covered** (35 assertions). Note the engine's rule: **no partial credit anywhere** — a 2-mark item answered half-right earns zero (Y5 Q11, Q15, Q25, Q31). Existing rule, unchanged.
- **4 open findings on 78 items**: Y5 Q20 (number-line highlights fall between ticks), Y3 Q26 and Y5 Q36 (answer unit not cued), Y5 Q33 (unit ambiguous). I earlier reported ten, including six screen-reader findings; five of those were my error — I had generalised `BarChartRenderer`'s behaviour to the line and pie renderers, which already expose their data. The checklist records the retraction rather than quietly editing it.
- **No item carries `approvedBy`.** Of the 46 pins resolving to a manifest, none has `humanApproval`/`approvedBy`; 32 have no manifest file. **Nothing here records or implies approval.**
- Reviewer route `/dev/family-beta-review` renders both papers through the same renderers a child uses, behind the papers' fail-closed gate (verified: 200 with the flag, 404 without, while public pages still serve).

## Blockers

- **Credentials.** `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` → 401; no DEV DB-owner URL, no writer password, no `EXAM_WRITE_DB_CA`, no `RECOVERY_GRANT_SECRET` — none of those four exists in the Vercel project for any target. **No migration was read or applied; no hosted verification ran.** Every box in §5–§7 is marked BLOCKED, not ticked.
- **Human content approval** on the 78 items.

Preview isolation verified: production deploys only from `main`, this branch deploys as Preview (`target: null`), and the review flag is scoped to `target: preview` **and** this branch alone (env id `Q1qdssAxhMfNJeb3` — delete when the review ends).

commits.messageBody:
…assessment integrity)

A signed-in student could call public.create_exam_session and
public.record_exam_attempt directly over PostgREST, because both are
SECURITY DEFINER and were granted to `authenticated` so the routes could call
them with the learner's own JWT. The first accepts a caller-chosen question
list and config (a one-question "full NAPLAN paper", even non-existent ids);
the second stores a caller-chosen result (a forged 100%). The routes scored
correctly; the functions behind them did not require the caller to be a route.

Interim fix consistent with ADR-005 (Amendment E), without the cutover:

- 20261031090000 (additive): role mindmosaic_exam_writer (LOGIN, no
  superuser/createdb/createrole/replication, NOBYPASSRLS, NOINHERIT, no table
  privilege) and server-only create_exam_session_for / record_exam_attempt_for
  that take the student id as an argument and keep every original check
  (role gate, ownership, expiry, unique-violation). Executable by the writer
  role only; anon/authenticated/PUBLIC/service_role revoked by name because
  default privileges grant new functions to them.
- 20261031090100 (breaking for the previous app): revokes both legacy
  functions from anon, authenticated and PUBLIC across every overload found in
  the catalogue, and asserts the outcome. Refuses to run without 090000.
- src/server/exam-write/legacy-exam-writes.ts is the one module holding
  EXAM_WRITE_DB_URL; the create, submit and onboarding routes pass the student
  id they just authenticated and fail closed with 503 if it is unset.

Tests: new tests/rls/exam-write-lockdown.test.ts (direct-RPC exploits denied,
no direct-write or other-RPC bypass, legitimate path, writer-role privilege
set); unit tests for forged-body and fail-closed behaviour; the boundary test
now covers the new credential and forbids calls to the revoked names.

Existing tests that asserted the vulnerable contract were rewritten, not
weakened: they now perform the same writes through the _for functions and keep
every behavioural assertion (ownership, immutability, duplicates, MM002/3/4).
The migration registry no longer asserts that `authenticated` can execute the
legacy functions; the inverse is asserted on the new entry.

Rollout order and rollback: docs/runbooks/legacy-exam-write-lockdown.md.

…eset access, error focus

Emailed links reach the app as a PKCE ?code (works only in the browser that requested it), a ?token_hash
(verifyOtp, works on any device) or an implicit #access_token fragment. The confirm and reset screens handled only
the first, so a parent who signed up on a laptop and opened the email on a phone saw "Link expired or invalid" with
a raw GoTrue "PKCE code verifier not found" message.

- /auth/confirm and /auth/reset accept all three shapes; token_hash and fragment links verify without a verifier.
- The PKCE verifier error becomes a plain-language explanation.
- /auth/reset opened with no link and no session no longer shows a password form that cannot work; it explains how
  to request a link. Signed-in users and valid links still get the form.
- Credentials are removed from the address bar once consumed.
- Problem states move focus to their heading (tabIndex -1) so keyboard and screen-reader users are told.

Existing reset tests that assumed the form appeared with no session now establish one; no assertion was removed.

…omed second code exchange

Recovery proof
- A session is no proof of recovery. The reset form opens only when the server accepts the access token (getUser) AND
  either (a) this tab recorded the recovery moment for this exact session_id (the SDK emitted PASSWORD_RECOVERY / our
  verifyOtp(type=recovery) succeeded; sessionStorage marker, 1h window) or (b) the SDK-reported authentication methods
  include a recent `recovery` entry (links delivered by GET /verify). `otp`, `password`, `email/signup` and `magiclink`
  are never accepted. Measured on the local GoTrue: verifyOtp(recovery) is recorded as `otp`, PKCE/implicit recovery as
  `recovery`, signup as `email/signup`, magic link as `magiclink`.
- Replaces the paused agent's isRecoveryContext, which read `amr` from the Session object (it has no such field).
- The recovery session is ended after the password changes.

Confirmation
- The browser client exchanges `?code=` by itself while initialising and consumes the code verifier, so the app's own
  second exchange failed ("code verifier not found") on a valid same-browser link. confirmEmail now first accepts a
  server-validated signup session created moments ago, never an older ordinary session.

Tests: unit coverage for each refused session type, server rejection, stale sessions, marker reload and cross-session
refusal; e2e covers same-browser and cross-device (token_hash) confirmation and recovery, reuse, cold and ordinary-session
access against an isolated local stack with a real mail catcher.

…ound grant

The reset page used a client-side sessionStorage marker and called Supabase's update-user API
directly, so the proof of recovery was only as strong as the browser. The server now verifies
the recovery token itself and issues a short-lived HttpOnly SameSite=Strict grant bound to the
user and Auth session; POST /api/auth/recovery/password accepts a new password only with that
grant, a same-origin Origin, a JSON body and a per-grant CSRF token, then signs the user out
globally. PKCE and implicit links are not exchanged a second time. The recovery template
puts the token in the URL fragment so it is in no request log. The runbooks are corrected:
legacy EXECUTE stays revoked, NOLOGIN alone is not a suspension, and no answer-saving promise
is made. This protects the application's reset path only; Supabase Auth's own update-user
API is outside it and is documented and tested as such.

Recovery grant claims (migration 20261102090000, not applied to any hosted project):
- each claim carries a fencing token; release needs the caller's own token, so an old
  claimant cannot release a newer claim
- claim records a digest of auth.users.encrypted_password; a lapsed claim whose password
  changed becomes spent, never re-claimable; release is refused once the hash changed
- ambiguous Auth answers (network, abort, 5xx, 408) are resolved against the database
  (resolve_recovery_claim) and never released on a guess; only a definitive 4xx releases
- 22 SQL tests incl. 12-connection races; 44 route tests incl. lease/takeover/fencing

commits.messageBody:
Review of ddd3d043..759fadbe against the required verification properties found
three ways the workflow could report a green run that did not prove what it claims.

1. The non-local-target guard listed connection variables by name and so missed
   SCORING_DB_URL, PROJECTION_DB_URL and CONTENT_ANSWER_WRITER_DB_URL, which are
   real connections (src/server/scoring/*, src/server/assessment/target-session-writes.ts).
   It now matches by shape (*_DB_URL, DATABASE_URL, *SUPABASE_URL), so a newly
   added connection is covered without editing the guard, and asserts
   NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL explicitly, because the loop can only reject values
   that are set.

2. "E2E public (full)" had no `if: always()`, so it was skipped whenever an
   earlier step failed - including "Summarise authenticated suite", which fails
   exactly when the authenticated suite had failures. The public suite must still
   run when the authenticated one fails; the final gate keeps the result red.

3. The keyboard-walkthrough x5 run and its summary sat inside one
   continue-on-error step whose outcome was not in the final gate, so a failing
   repeat, or a missing or empty report, could not fail the workflow. The summary
   is now its own step with --require-spec, and both outcomes are gated.

Also creates evidence/ up front so every later `tee evidence/...` works even if a
suite step dies early. No test or assertion changed.

whenever they were absent from process.env, and threw on ENOENT if the file

The green family-beta-verify run on 50916415 had two gaps that made it prove
less than it appeared to.

1. Twenty of the ninety authenticated tests SKIPPED, and they were the whole
   email path: e2e/auth/email-confirmation-and-recovery.spec.ts and
   e2e/auth/password-recovery-security.spec.ts call test.skip(!MAIL) when
   E2E_MAILPIT_URL is unset, and the workflow never set it. So the run proved
   nothing about email confirmation or password recovery, which is what this
   candidate exists for. `supabase start` already runs the catcher on the
   runner ([inbucket], port 56324, Mailpit API) and e2e/fixtures/mailpit.ts
   already defaults to that URL, so this only needed the variable. These tests
   now pass or fail; they can no longer silently skip. No hosted target is
   added.

2. The repeated keyboard coverage targeted the wrong spec. The observed flake
   was in the PUBLIC suite -- e2e/a11y-auth-pages.spec.ts "sign-in keyboard
   walkthrough" failed its first attempt and passed on retry -- while the x5
   repeat covered the authenticated parent dashboard, which never flaked. A
   second repeat step runs the public walkthroughs x5 with --retries=0, gated
   by --require-spec a11y-auth-pages, and both its steps join the final gate.
   With retries off a flake fails the step, so a real focus-order defect is
   now distinguishable from a one-off.

commits.messageBody:
…answer claim

Adds a per-area table to the rollout checklist saying, for each listed
beta-impacting area, what it actually rests on and where the evidence is,
separating "proved by tests that ran" from "control exists in code but its
hosted configuration was never read".

One area was not covered and is now stated plainly: student PIN abuse
protection. A student signs in via signInWithPassword(alias, pin) with a
6-digit PIN and there is NO application-level lockout or attempt counter. What
protects it is that the alias email is derived from an 8-character ~40-bit
secret login code that is never stored as a mapping, so an attacker must guess
the code as well as the PIN, plus Supabase's sign_in_sign_ups throttle (30 per
5 minutes per IP in config.toml). The hosted DEV throttle was never read and
local config.toml values do not apply to a hosted project, so this is recorded
as bounded, tied to A5.

Also corrects a claim I had put on the reviewer page and in the component
doc comment. It said these pages "never receive an answer key as a client
prop" - technically true, since the expected answer is passed as a formatted
string rather than a key object, but misleading: the reveal is client state,
so the answer and explanation ARE in the page payload whether or not the
button is pressed. Verified by grepping the rendered HTML. Both now say so,
and say why that is acceptable only because the route is gated to
non-production deployments.

Rendering verified locally against a production build: /dev/family-beta-review
and /year3 both 200 (36 cards, 21 rendered SVG visuals, correct per-item
findings), and both 404 on a server without FAMILY_BETA_FIXED_PAPERS_PREVIEW
while the public pages still serve 200.

commits.messageBody:
…ct a wrong finding

I reported six Year 5 items as unanswerable with a screen reader, on the
grounds that the chart renderers mark every data mark aria-hidden and expose
only altText, and that those six have generic alt text naming none of their
plotted values. I had checked that against BarChartRenderer and then assumed
the other two renderers matched. They did not:

  - LineGraphRenderer already renders an sr-only <ul> of every point's label,
    x and y, so Q8, Q16, Q26 and Q42 were never inaccessible.
  - PieChartRenderer already exposes each segment's label, value and
    percentage in a visible legend, so Q32 was never inaccessible.
  - BarChartRenderer was the real gap - the only chart renderer with no
    accessible data equivalent. That affected Q23, and any other bar-chart
    item whose alt text happens not to recite its values.

So rather than hand the owner a design decision that did not exist,
BarChartRenderer now carries the same sr-only list as LineGraphRenderer, with
two tests. That closes the gap for every bar chart in the application instead
of for this beta's single item. It states the data, not the answer - the same
line the other two renderers already drew.

CHART-ALT-NO-DATA is therefore removed from the findings module rather than
left in with no members, and the pinned expectation drops from 10 findings to
4. The checklist records the retraction explicitly instead of quietly editing
it away.

Also fixes a real omission this candidate introduced, caught by CI's
navigation-graph test on 99127c60 (core failed; rls/e2e/e2e-auth passed):
/dev/family-beta-review's only links were template literals, so it was a
screen with no way out except the marketing site. It now carries an explicit
link out, and the route is listed on /dev/routes under a new Dev tools group.

CI evidence added for the student journey. On a34fd6f8 the authenticated
suite's one flake was student-exam-session.spec.ts - code+PIN sign-in, start a
timed exam, autosave, resume after refresh - which is the exact journey both
children will take. A retry-pass is not adequate evidence for that, so a
student exam journey x5 step runs it with retries off, gated by
--require-spec, and joins the final gate.

Local: typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, build clean, 406/406 suites and
7142/7142 tests pass.

commits.messageBody:
… defect

The student-exam-journey x5 gate I added did its job on e5b02db3 and found a
real defect, and in doing so exposed a gating hole that had been there since
this workflow was written.

1. GATING HOLE. Every summarise-playwright.mjs step ran as
   `node ... | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" evidence/....md`, and GitHub's
   default shell is `bash -e`, not `bash -eo pipefail`. A pipeline exits with
   its LAST command's status, so the summariser's exit 1 was replaced by
   tee's exit 0. On e5b02db3 the summary printed "tests: 5 passed: 4
   failed: 1" with a Failures section and its step still reported
   journey_summary=success. That was true of all five summarise steps, so the
   requirement that an empty or failing report cannot count as passing was
   never actually enforced; the failure only surfaced because the playwright
   step itself sets pipefail and the gate checks both. All five now set it.
   Earlier runs' SUITE results stand (those steps had pipefail); their report
   checks were simply not load-bearing.

2. OPEN DEFECT, not masked. e2e/auth/student-exam-session.spec.ts:56 failed
   1 of 5 with `strict mode violation: getByTestId('start-exam') resolved to
   2 elements` - one enabled ("Review instructions"), one disabled. So the
   page transiently holds two start controls, one hydrated and one still
   pre-hydration. ExamConfigurator declares that testid once and the route
   renders the component once, so these are two live copies.

   Established: the server HTML contains exactly one; a direct unauthenticated
   load never duplicates (20/20 local runs polling from navigation-commit, no
   console or page errors); it needs the authenticated path; useHydrated uses
   the correct useSyncExternalStore snapshot pattern and is not a mismatch
   source. NOT established: the root cause - the authenticated path needs the
   local Supabase stack and cannot be reproduced on this Windows host.

   So it is left failing rather than papered over with .first(), a
   toHaveCount wait, a retry or a longer timeout. Instead the next run is made
   diagnostic: the journey repeat runs with --trace=on, and its test-results
   are copied to evidence/journey-test-results immediately after the step
   rather than in the shared collect step at the end - on e5b02db3 the public
   suite reused test-results/ and overwrote this failure's error-context.md
   and trace before upload, which is why that run diagnosed nothing.

Checklist updated: status is NO-GO on three things now, this defect included,
and the premature "journey PASSED" line (which I had read off the step's
continue-on-error conclusion rather than its outcome) is corrected.

commits.messageBody:
family-beta-verify was GREEN on 35474d87 while the duplicate start-exam
defect fired twice on that very run. In the full authenticated suite
e2e/auth/student-exam-session.spec.ts failed, failed again on retry #1 and
passed only on retry #2 (attempts: 3), both failures with the same
`getByTestId('start-exam') resolved to 2 elements`. The job was green because
summarise-playwright.mjs reports flaky without failing on it.

The isolated x5 repeat I added earlier passed 5/5 on the same run, so it is a
WEAKER detector than the full suite: the repeat runs against a warm, idle
server, while in the full suite the test runs after ~70 others, which widens
the hydration race window. Keeping both is right, but the full suite's result
is the one that matters and it was being discarded.

So summarise-playwright.mjs gains --no-flaky-spec <substring>: a retry-pass on
a named spec now exits 1 and is printed under its own heading. The
authenticated step passes --no-flaky-spec student-exam-session. For a journey
the product depends on, a retry-pass is a failure.

Verified against real reports rather than by assertion, replaying the artifacts
of the green run:
  - 35474d87's own pw-auth.json through the new check -> exit 1, naming the
    spec (it would have been red).
  - its clean x5 journey report -> exit 0.
  - its public report, which is flaky on a DIFFERENT spec -> exit 0.
  - an empty report -> exit 1, unchanged.

Confirmed occurrences of this one error: a34fd6f8 (1), e5b02db3 (1 of 5 in the
repeat), 35474d87 (2 in the full suite). At least four across three runs; it
is not a flake. Root cause still not established - it needs the authenticated
path, and 32 local attempts across hard and soft navigation produced zero
duplicates - so it stays open and unmasked.

commits.messageBody:
POST /api/exam/session has always deduped on `idempotencyKey` and answered
409 `idempotency_key_reused`, but NO caller ever sent one: startServerExam
posted `{ config, bankId }`, so the route fell back to
`idempotencyKey ?? crypto.randomUUID()` and minted a fresh key per request.
The dedupe was unreachable from the application, and two concurrent POSTs
each created a real session, leaving an orphan attached to the student.

ExamConfigurator.handleStart does guard with `isStarting || isCreating` and
disables the button, but that is React state - a UI guard, not a request
guard. It cannot help a request duplicated in transit, nor a programmatic
double-invoke within one tick.

Two changes in the store, which is where the request is issued:
  - one stable idempotencyKey per start attempt, so the server can recognise
    a duplicate of that single request;
  - coalescing, so a concurrent second call joins the in-flight promise
    instead of issuing a request at all.

The key is minted per user-initiated attempt and the slot is released however
the attempt settles - including a thrown network error - so retrying after a
genuine failure gets a fresh key rather than replaying a spent one into a 409
and locking the student out.

Five unit tests cover: a key is sent at all; a fresh key per attempt; three
concurrent starts issue exactly ONE fetch and all resolve true; and the slot
is released after both a non-ok response and a thrown error.

Also closes the last two unguarded pipelines in family-beta-verify: the build
identity steps read `.next/BUILD_ID` inside a command substitution and piped
through `tee`, so a missing file printed "BUILD_ID=" and still exited 0 -
recording a blank identity as though it were evidence. Both now set pipefail
and assert the file exists. The only pipeline left without pipefail is an
`ls | head` listing, where truncation is the intent.

commits.messageHeadline: fix(exam): concurrent starts cannot create duplicate exam sessions

commits.messageBody:
student-exam-session.spec.ts asserted
`expect(getByTestId("start-exam")).toBeVisible()`. getByTestId matches nodes
hidden from both layout and the accessibility tree, so that conflated "one
start control" with "one DOM node carrying this test id" and failed
intermittently on Linux CI with `strict mode violation: ... resolved to 2
elements` - one enabled, one disabled.

Classification. The second copy is hidden, not a second usable button. Both
render the same static label ("Review instructions" - there is no
pre-hydration label variant), yet Playwright aliased only the first as
getByRole('button', { name: 'Review instructions' }) and fell back to
.nth(1) for the second. A role+name selector is only unique when the other
node is excluded from role matching, which is exactly what being hidden from
the a11y tree does. The server HTML also contains exactly one.

That is an inference, not a local demonstration, and it is labelled as such
in the spec: the duplicate never reproduced locally in ~102 attempts - 20
unauthenticated hard navigations, 12 soft navigations, 60 authenticated
navigations polling the DOM from navigation-commit, and 10 full spec runs
(whose 3 failures were a different, Windows-local sign-in stall, with zero
occurrences of the strict-mode error). It is CI-timing-specific.

The replacement is strictly stronger, so this is not a locator papered over a
bug:
  - exactly one `[data-testid="start-exam"]:visible`
  - exactly one `getByRole('button', { name: 'Review instructions' })`
  - that one is visible
and the click now targets the visible control. If a second copy is ever
genuinely visible, or genuinely reachable by a screen reader, these counts
fail loudly rather than the suite passing on a retry. The --no-flaky-spec
gate stays in place over this spec.

Verified 6/6 with --repeat-each=6 --retries=0 against a local Supabase stack,
on a build that also carries the start-session coalescing change.
